svg.title: How a call flows
svg.desc: One pickup call as a transcript, in three columns: what is said on the phone, the stations the sentence passes, and what the code does with it. The caller's words pass the access, Asterisk, the ear, the conversation core and the LLM; the agent's reply passes the LLM, the core, the mouth, Asterisk and the access. The caller orders: get_service_status and search_menu, one tool per hop, at most six, each run by the core against Postgres; the LLM has no line to a tool or the database. With the caller's name the core runs draft_order, every price from Postgres. The agent reads the draft back word for word. Only after the caller's yes does the core run confirm. The agent confirms; meanwhile the order shows on the tablet, and the slip prints after the team's approval, in primary mode up to the amount limit at once. Set apart, the ways to the team: when the AI is unsure, hears a complaint no rule covers or the model fails, the team phone rings while the restaurant is open; after hours, when the caller's number is known, a callback waits on the tablet. When the service voice fails, the exchange rings the team phone. Each station's edge shows whether it is built, in progress or planned.
